threads.body: This failure finalizer only catches `Exception`, but async cancellation raises `asyncio.CancelledError`, which inherits directly from `BaseException`. If snapshot adoption or partial-response extraction raises cancellation, control exits before `invocation.fail(exc)` and before the finalized flag is set, leaving telemetry unfinished or permitting a second finalization. Catch `BaseException` for this best-effort telemetry block while continuing to pass the original `exc` to `fail`.

threads.body: This best-effort capture path can also raise other `BaseException` subclasses (for example `KeyboardInterrupt`, `SystemExit`, or `GeneratorExit`). Because the shared stream wrapper marks itself finalized before calling `_fail`, one of those exceptions escapes here before `invocation.fail(exc)`, leaving the span unfinished and replacing the original stream error. Catch `BaseException` for this telemetry-only section so all capture failures are logged and the original `exc` is still used for finalization, as required by the [instrumentation exception-handling rule](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-genai/blob/main/.github/instructions/instrumentation.instructions.md#5-exception-handling).

- https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-genai/blob/main/instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-genai-anthropic/tests/test_async_messages.py#L716-L747

In `test_sync_messages_stream_interrupted_mid_iteration`, `ErrorInjectingStreamDelegate` currently fails on `self._count == 1` (right after `message_start` before content deltas arrive). 

We can:
1. Have `ErrorInjectingStreamDelegate` fail after a few chunks (`if self._count >= 3:`) so content deltas are received.
2. Run with content capture enabled (`instrument_with_content` or parametrize `capture_content`).
3. Assert that the resulting span preserves the partial `gen_ai.output.messages` and `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`.
